processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental alloys (Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C) were melted in an induction furnace.
Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched; this is the parent process (proc_solution-treated-1250c-35min-wq) of the 700 °C annealing.
The materials were then cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples.

Isothermal holding at 700 °C was one of four annealing treatments (500, 700, 900, 1050 °C). The holding time is not explicitly reported. In the Ni-free alloy the matrix remained γ + α and needle-like κ-carbides formed within α instead of the B2 stringer bands seen in the Ni-containing alloy.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex γ (austenite) + α (ferrite) microstructure containing coarse FeAl-type B2 particles (2–4 μm) and κ-carbide precipitates (nano-sized cuboid κ in γ and needle-like κ in α); the α phase is retained (not replaced by B2 stringer bands, unlike the Ni-containing alloy).

microstructure_list.region: matrix (austenite γ grains and ferrite α)

phases_present.morphology: nano-sized cuboid blocks in γ; needle-like in α
coarse particles (2–4 μm) in the matrix

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation carried out at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s⁻¹ up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times in arrays of 50–70 indentations across the region of interest. The technique yields a compound hardness value of the matrix with particles.
Mn content of the needle-like κ-carbide formed in α, measured/derived for the Ni-free alloy annealed at 700 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma FE-SEM operated at 20 kV, fitted with high-speed X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS); specimens polished and etched in 5% nital solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Observation of the microstructure (matrix phases, B2 stringer bands/particles, grain-boundary precipitates).
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to image the micro-scale microstructure; the micrographs presented (Fig. 2) show the Ni-containing sample, while the Ni-free alloy followed a similar trend except that α + needle-like κ-carbides (rather than B2 stringer bands) were observed at 500 and 700 °C.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) — bright-field imaging and selected-area diffraction patterns (SADP)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2000FX TEM; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at an applied potential of 25 V
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterization of the ordered phases (κ-carbides and B2) at the nano-scale via SADP and bright-field imaging.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to identify/observe nano-sized ordered precipitates (cuboid κ in γ, disc-like B2 in α).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s⁻¹ up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement repeated at least 25 times in arrays of 50–70 indentations across the region of interest
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine the (compound) hardness of individual phases and combinations of phases because isolated nano-sized precipitates cannot be measured individually.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Ni-free alloy annealed at 700 °C: γ + κ hardness = 7 GPa and α + needle-like κ hardness = 6.7 GPa; κ precipitated at 700 °C contained higher Mn (≈24.8 wt.%) than at 500 °C (≈18.4 wt.%).

computational_details.simulation_method: First-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT), spin-polarized generalized gradient approximation (GGA-PBE); lattice parameter and elastic constants of κ-carbide computed as a function of Mn content
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials created based on a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Brillouin zone integrations by an 18 × 18 × 18 Monkhorst–Pack grid for structure optimization; real-space grid with a 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded to 600 Ryd; 30 × 30 × 30 grid with 60 Ryd cut-off for the electronic DOS and formation energy; bulk modulus obtained by fitting simulated unit-cell volumes with a Murnaghan equation of state; dynamical matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation; DOS by the tetrahedron method with a 30 × 30 × 30 mesh
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameters compared with experimental values (Fig. 6) and found in good agreement; calculated elastic constants confirm the experimentally observed increase in hardness of κ with increasing Mn content (Fe3AlC < Mn3AlC).

analytical_models.equation_role: Fit of total energy vs unit-cell volume to obtain the bulk modulus
analytical_models.model_note: Used to calculate the bulk modulus from simulated unit-cell volumes (b0024).
Practical elastic parameter derived from calculated elastic constants.

analytical_models.equation_role: C11 and C44 from the [100] longitudinal/transverse sound velocities (eqs 1–2) and C12 from the [111] longitudinal velocity (eq 3)
analytical_models.model_note: First of the two methods used to evaluate elastic constants.

analytical_models.equation_role: Volume-conserving orthorhombic distortion to obtain C11 − C12 (eq 5) and monoclinic distortion to obtain C44 (eq 7)
analytical_models.model_note: Second method (values given in parentheses in Table 3).

unmapped_findings: Alloy naming inconsistency: the alloy is written as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C in the abstract, introduction, methods and conclusions, but Tables 1 and 2 label the same Ni-free alloy as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C (0.5C); this appears to be a typographical inconsistency (0.8 vs 0.5 C).
The annealing holding time at 700 °C is not explicitly reported anywhere in the paper; only the temperature (one of 500, 700, 900, 1050 °C) is given.

A previous study (ref. 11) reported that at lower annealing temperatures the materials had low ductility (elongation ≈10%) and that increasing the annealing temperature improved the strength–ductility balance in both grades due to removal of κ-carbides and formation of nano-sized B2 discs in the ferrite; these values are not specific to the 700 °C Ni-free sample and no direction/uncertainty is given.
The nano-indentation technique used cannot measure isolated nano-sized precipitates, so reported values are compound (matrix + particle) hardness values rather than true single-phase κ hardness.

In the Ni-free alloy at 500–700 °C the α (ferrite) phase was retained (containing α + needle-like κ-carbides), in contrast to the Ni-containing alloy where the α phase was replaced by B2 stringer bands at these temperatures.
